newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's air cargo market ignores seasonal shifts.
newsitem.headline: Russia's air cargo market ignores seasonal shifts.

text.p: Russia's air cargo market was stable in spite of the peak holiday season, and rates have changed little during last three weeks, a Reuters survey showed.
Maria Shakova, Sheremetyevo-Cargo's manager, told Reuters the market was stable in July.
"We have even had a few more shipments in July compared with the previous month," she said, adding that rates were unchanged.
"But some forwarders offered dumping rates as usual."
Shakova said her company's export shipments had increased by up to 13 percent in the first half of this year after a ten percent increase in first six months of 1996.
"This tendency may continue," she said.
Lilia Sirbu, chief executive for Icaros International Cargo Service, Aeroflot's cargo agent, said export shipments were more active during last three weeks.
"Russian companies made orders to ship cargo from Russia to India and U.S. destinations in spite of customs difficulties at the Sheremetyevo airport," she said.
Ilya Maslennikov, senior cargo manager at forwarding firm Eruslan, agent for Aeroflot and some Western airlines, also said the market was stable.

"It is ignoring seasonal fluctuations, but we hope August and September will be more active than July," he said, adding that activity at the Sheremetyevo airport was low due to high handling rates there.
"More and more clients prefer to avoid this airport, using trucks to deliver cargo from door-to-door."
Maslennikov also said air cargo shipments inside Russia were becoming more attractive for carriers and forwarders.
"Competition on domestic cargo routes is weaker compared with international flights...and many carriers are trying to get involved in this promising business," he said.
But Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow, saw a thin market in July.
"We had more shipments this time last year. The market is unpredictable, but we hope it will be more active next month," he said.
Mordvinov said his company had begun sea shipment operations with heavy cargo from St Petersburg.
"For some clients is more profitable to send heavy cargo by ship from Russia to Asia and South America," he said, adding that this business has a promising future.
Sergei Mochalov, TCT-Cargo senior manager, said active destinations during the last three weeks were Moscow to the United States, Khabarovsk and Novosibirsk.
"Domestic flights are becaming more profitable. We hope to have more shipments on domestic flights (than international) in August," he said.
Marina Samokhvalova, Trans-Charter's manager, said domestic flights were particularly active. "Demand is increasing there."
Shakova said 50 percent of Sheremetyevo-Cargo's export shipments were currently to European destinations, 40 percent to Asia and 10 percent to the U.S., South America and Africa.
Sirbu said Icaros was bidding for an order to deliver 120 tonnes of Danish humanitarian aid from Moscow to Ulan Bator in Mongolia in the end of August.
"We would use three Ilyushin-76 freighters for this," she added.
